A standard value with no matching token (`noToken`) is a real design-system gap worth publishing, but it does NOT excuse the portal. _what: The SAMAVESH house standard: the baseline a MoSJE portal is audited against when it has no design frames of its own. Generated — never hand-edited. Regenerate with `python3 tools/design-audit/house/derive.py`.

chrome._what: The components every page of the estate composes. A portal missing one of these is missing estate chrome, which is a finding a token diff cannot see.

contract._modeNote: The baseline is the UNION across every brand/mode/surface block, so a build in one mode is never convicted for a value another mode publishes. Deliberately permissive.

evidence._bindingNote: Share of sampled fills bound to a Figma variable rather than set as a literal. A literal that merely EQUALS a token is not bound to it (documentation-ds-linkage.md). This is the design FILE's own adoption figure and is not a measure of any build.
evidence.source: house/figma_histogram.js run once per page against Figma file evmNmlK8g4VYwJVu2FwSGV (MoSJE Portal — Handoff), via the Figma MCP, 2026-09-12. All 12 pages of the file, no sampling of pages. Within a page, TEXT nodes are capped at 4,000 and container nodes at 6,000 — every page except Login/Signup hits the container cap, so per-page counts are a census of the first N nodes in document order, not of the whole page. Frequencies are therefore comparable across axes within a page and indicative, not exact, across pages.

#000000.why: Pure black text. The file's own dominant ink is #1f2937 by an order of magnitude, and pure black is in neither the file's ramp nor the token contract.

#d9d9d9.why: Figma's default rectangle fill — an unstyled placeholder shape on roughly 4,000 nodes, never a colour decision.
